# neptune

Amazon Neptune Database and Neptune Analytics - Gremlin/openCypher/SPARQL access, explain/profile plans (non-native steps, unbounded estimates, all-label scans), Analytics algorithms and vector topK, plus cluster encryption posture from dumps.

## Detected anti-patterns

### `AF-DATA-013` — Graph traversal/query without a limit (medium)

A Gremlin traversal with no limit()/range()/tail()/next()/count() on the chain, or an openCypher/SPARQL read without LIMIT (Neptune or Neo4j), returns an unbounded graph result — memory cost scales with the graph.


Remediation: Bound traversals with .limit(n)/.range(a,b) and add LIMIT to query strings.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/access-graph-gremlin.html

### `AF-STORE-004` — Neptune cluster storage is not encrypted (critical)

Same posture as DocumentDB — `StorageEncrypted: false` is a declared fact about the cluster, not a guess.

Remediation: Recreate the cluster encrypted (snapshot-restore migration path) with a customer-managed key.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/encrypt.html

### `AF-GDB-007` — SPARQL property path with + or * and no bound (medium)

A property path such as :knows+ or <p>* follows the predicate to any depth; on RDF graphs with cycles or hubs the closure is large.


Remediation: Replace with fixed-length paths or bounded unions, and add LIMIT.

Reference: https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-query/#propertypaths

### `AF-GDB-009` — Neptune Analytics algorithm with no scoping MATCH (medium)

CALL neptune.algo.* with no preceding MATCH runs the algorithm over the whole graph; memory and latency follow graph size.


Remediation: Bind source nodes with MATCH (and a label/property filter) before CALL, or run it as a scheduled job.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune-analytics/latest/userguide/algorithms.html

### `AF-GDB-010` — Neptune Analytics vector search without topK (medium)

A neptune.algo.vectors.* call with no topK parameter leaves the result size to the default instead of the request's need.


Remediation: Declare topK sized to the response page.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune-analytics/latest/userguide/vector-similarity.html

### `AF-GDB-020` — Plan falls back to non-native TinkerPop steps (medium)

Neptune explain reports steps 'not converted into Neptune steps'; from that point the whole traversal runs in the slower TinkerPop engine.


Remediation: Rewrite the unsupported step (fold/unfold, lambdas, some predicates) with native equivalents.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/gremlin-explain-api.html

### `AF-GDB-021` — Plan carries an unbounded cardinality estimate (medium)

estimatedCardinality=INFINITY or a maximal rangeCountEstimate means the optimizer had no bound for a pattern; it will scan.


Remediation: Add a label/id anchor or a selective property filter before the pattern.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/gremlin-explain-api.html

### `AF-GDB-022` — Plan warns about the number of predicates (low)

Neptune flags queries whose cost depends on the number of distinct predicates (edge labels/properties), typical of unlabeled reverse steps.


Remediation: Name edge labels in in()/both() steps.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/gremlin-explain-api.html

### `AF-GDB-023` — Plan scans all labels (medium)

A DFEPipelineScan/PipelineJoin over label 'ALL' reads every node or edge before filtering.


Remediation: Add the node label to the pattern (n:Label) so the scan uses the label index.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/access-graph-opencypher-explain.html
